name: Gufic BioSciences Ltd
tagline: Vertically-integrated lyophilised-injectables and NDDS maker whose big Indore capex cycle is done (maintenance-only capex now), whose European-GMP overhang is resolving (Navsari already EU-GMP; Indore inspection completed Dec 2025, certification expected imminently), with a GLP-1 CMO tie-up with Hetero ramping from Q2/Q3 FY27 — margins have inflected to ~18% for two straight quarters with Indore still only 30% utilised, but the stock trades ~65x trailing earnings
business_overview: Gufic BioSciences is a vertically integrated sterile-injectables company spanning API manufacturing to formulations, specialising in lyophilised injectables and advanced drug-delivery systems (NDDS — depot, microsphere, liposomal), plus a GLP-1 CMO partnership with Hetero and an aesthetics business (India's #2 botulinum-toxin franchise, now adding an in-licensed Canadian dermal-filler portfolio). Its large Indore plant (commissioned Oct 2024) can generate ~Rs 675-700 Cr of revenue at 75%+ utilisation versus ~30% in FY26.
fundamentals_table: Revenue Rs 940.5 Cr; EBITDA Rs 152.9 Cr (~16.3% margin); PAT Rs 63.2 Cr; Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 18.22% vs 12.99% YoY
Revenue from ops Rs 260.8 Cr (+15% YoY); EBITDA Rs 47.2 Cr (+42.2%), margin 18.09% vs 14.6%; PAT Rs 22.5 Cr (+~85% YoY, +70.7% consol), PAT margin 8.61% vs 5.3%; EPS Rs 2.22 vs Rs 1.30

Commissioned Oct 2024; ~30% utilisation FY26, targeting 40-45% by FY27-end; ~Rs 675-700 Cr revenue potential at 75%+; new NDDS capabilities (depot/microsphere, liposomal antifungal) nearing completion
Now maintenance-only (~Rs 20 Cr/yr) — the big build cycle is complete
D/E 0.61 (Mar 2026, below 10-yr median 0.79); trailing P/E ~62-65x (pharma avg ~29x)
fundamentals_narrative: Trailing quality is still unspectacular (ROCE ~12.2%, ROE ~10%) at a rich ~65x trailing P/E, but the operating picture has improved on several fronts this pass. (1) The big capex cycle is done — capex has shifted to maintenance-only (~Rs 20 Cr), so the large Indore lyophilised-injectables plant is built and now a harvest asset, at only ~30% utilisation with ~Rs 675-700 Cr of latent revenue on a Rs 940 Cr base. (2) The European-GMP overhang that had gated conviction is resolving: Navsari already holds EU-GMP / WHO-GMP / Health Canada, and Indore completed its EU-GMP inspection in December 2025 with certification expected in Q1 FY27. (3) Margins have inflected — EBITDA margin ~18% in both Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 versus 13-15% previously — driven by operating leverage and a mix shift to NDDS/CMO, and management guides ~18% for FY27 and 20% by FY30. (4) A GLP-1 CMO partnership with Hetero (Hetero received approvals May 2026) had only residual Q1 revenue but is expected to ramp from Q2/Q3 FY27. International traction is building (approvals in 8 countries, a North America CMO+licensing deal, first Australian orders), and the aesthetics division adds an in-licensed Canadian filler portfolio launching Dec 2026/Jan 2027. Revenue growth in Q1 was a modest +15%, so the near-term story is earnings leverage on a fixed cost base rather than a topline surge.

verdict_headline: The GMP overhang that gated conviction is resolving, the capex cycle is done, and margins have inflected for two straight quarters — conviction up to Medium; still capped by a ~65x multiple and an early-stage Indore ramp
verdict_reasoning: Conviction had been explicitly held at Low-Medium 'pending resolution of the GMP overhang'. That is now materially de-risked: Navsari already holds EU-GMP/WHO-GMP/Health Canada, and Indore completed its EU-GMP inspection in Dec 2025 with certification expected Q1 FY27. Combined with the capex cycle turning to maintenance-only and EBITDA margin inflecting to ~18% across Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27, this warrants raising conviction to Medium.

four_box score rises to 3.5: tailwind upgraded weak->yes (Indore ramp 30%->75%+ with ~Rs 675-700 Cr latent revenue, GLP-1 CMO wave with Hetero, EU-GMP export unlock, capex now maintenance-only), tam yes, moat yes (vertically-integrated lyophilised/NDDS niche), valuation weak (~65x trailing, but a static multiple under-weights the operating leverage on a 30%-utilised plant). Score >= 3.0 keeps '10x-in-2-3-years' permitted.

The cap on conviction is valuation and execution timing: at ~65x trailing the multiple already prices meaningful growth, Indore utilisation is targeted at only 40-45% by FY27-end, and the GLP-1/Hetero revenue is guided rather than delivered.

No VP-trusted-tier user has independently corroborated the bull case; the strongest external conviction remains the IAS-2026 presenter's disclosed largest-position holding. Medium conviction; revisit on EU-GMP Indore issuance, a Q2/Q3 FY27 print showing GLP-1 revenue, and utilisation progress.
